returns: The converted long long. Throws std::invalid_argument if no conversion occurs and std::out_of_range for a range error; check position when the whole string must be consumed.

summary: Parse a numeric prefix from a string after optional whitespace and sign. The optional position reports how many characters were consumed; trailing characters are not an error by themselves. Integer conversions also accept an explicit base; base zero recognizes standard numeric prefixes.
signature: unsigned long stoul(const std::string& text, std::size_t* position = nullptr, int base = 10);

signature: unsigned long long stoull(const std::string& text, std::size_t* position = nullptr, int base = 10);

signature: float stof(const std::string& text, std::size_t* position = nullptr);

summary: Create a string representation of a numeric value. In C++17 the overloads use printf-style formatting; floating-point forms normally use six fractional digits and follow the current C locale. C++26 changes the formatting specification.
parameters: - `value`: an arithmetic value. Other signed, unsigned and floating overloads are available.
returns: A newly allocated string. These signatures show representative overloads.

summary: A non-owning, read-only view of a contiguous character sequence. It does not keep the referenced storage alive and need not be null-terminated. Do not retain a view into a destroyed or reallocated string. Available since C++17.
members:
- `size()`, `empty()`: query the view.
- `data()`: underlying pointer, not necessarily terminated.
- `substr()`, `remove_prefix()`, `remove_suffix()`: create or adjust views.
- `find()`, `compare()`: inspect characters without taking ownership.

summary: Find the first element for which a predicate is true, without changing the range.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class Predicate>
InputIt find_if(InputIt first, InputIt last, Predicate predicate);
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: input range.
- `predicate`: test that must not modify the element.
returns: An iterator to the first match, or last. At most N predicate calls.

summary: Count elements satisfying a predicate. The predicate must not modify inspected elements.
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: input range.
- `predicate`: classification test.
returns: The count of matching elements. Exactly N predicate calls.

summary: Test whether every element satisfies a predicate. An empty range satisfies the condition.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class Predicate>
bool all_of(InputIt first, InputIt last, Predicate predicate);
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: input range.
- `predicate`: non-modifying test.
returns: true if every test succeeds, otherwise false. At most N predicate calls.

summary: Test whether at least one element satisfies a predicate. An empty range produces false.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class Predicate>
bool any_of(InputIt first, InputIt last, Predicate predicate);
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: input range.
- `predicate`: non-modifying test.
returns: true if at least one test succeeds. At most N predicate calls.

summary: Test whether no element satisfies a predicate. An empty range produces true.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class Predicate>
bool none_of(InputIt first, InputIt last, Predicate predicate);
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: input range.
- `predicate`: non-modifying test.
returns: true if every test fails. At most N predicate calls.

summary: Copy a range forward into already available destination elements. It does not grow a container. The destination start must not lie inside the source range; use copy_backward for a rightward overlapping move.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class OutputIt>
OutputIt copy(InputIt first, InputIt last, OutputIt destination);
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: source range.
- `destination`: start of writable output with sufficient space.
returns: The output iterator after the last copied element. Exactly N assignments.

summary: Copy elements satisfying a predicate into available output storage, preserving their relative order. The source and output ranges must not overlap, and enough destination space must already exist.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class OutputIt, class Predicate>
OutputIt copy_if(InputIt first, InputIt last, OutputIt destination, Predicate predicate);
parameters: - Source range, writable destination and non-modifying predicate.
returns: The iterator after the copied elements. Exactly N predicate calls.

summary: Copy count elements into existing output storage. A nonpositive count performs no assignments. Do not rely on this algorithm for overlapping ranges.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class Size, class OutputIt>
OutputIt copy_n(InputIt first, Size count, OutputIt destination);
parameters:
- `first`: source start with enough readable elements.
- `count`: element count.
- `destination`: writable output start.
returns: The iterator after the copied elements. Exactly max(count, 0) assignments.

summary: Apply an operation and assign its result into each destination element. The unary overload can transform a range in place. Output storage must already exist, and evaluation order is not guaranteed.
signature:
template<class InputIt, class OutputIt, class Operation>
OutputIt transform(InputIt first, InputIt last, OutputIt destination, Operation operation);
parameters:
- Input range, writable output and transformation operation.
- The operation must not invalidate iterators or modify unrelated elements in the involved ranges.
returns: The output iterator after the last result. Exactly N operation applications.

summary: Move elements not equal to value toward the beginning, preserving their order. It does not erase container elements or change physical size. The tail after the returned logical end remains valid but has unspecified values.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class T>
ForwardIt remove(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, const T& value);
parameters:
- `[first, last)`: writable range.
- `value`: value to remove; avoid passing a reference to an element that the algorithm can overwrite.
returns: The new logical end. Erase the tail separately when using a container. Linear time.

summary: Move elements failing a predicate toward the beginning, preserving their relative order. This changes the logical range but does not erase storage or reduce a container size.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class Predicate>
ForwardIt remove_if(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, Predicate predicate);
parameters: - Writable range and a predicate that does not modify its argument.
returns: The new logical end; the remaining tail contains valid but unspecified values. Exactly N predicate calls.

summary: Remove consecutive equivalent values from the logical range, preserving the retained order. It does not remove non-adjacent duplicates or shrink a container; sort first only when reordering is acceptable.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt>
ForwardIt unique(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last);
parameters: - `[first, last)`: writable range; equality must be an equivalence relation.
returns: The new logical end. Erase the remaining tail separately for a container. Linear time.

summary: Assign newValue to every element equal to oldValue. The number and positions of elements do not change.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class T>
void replace(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, const T& oldValue, const T& newValue);
parameters: - Writable range and values to compare and assign. Avoid aliasing values with elements that can be overwritten.
returns: No return value. Exactly N comparisons.

summary: Assign a replacement value to elements satisfying a predicate. The range size and the order of other elements remain unchanged.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class Predicate, class T>
void replace_if(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, Predicate predicate, const T& newValue);
parameters: - Writable range, non-modifying predicate and replacement value.
returns: No return value. Exactly N predicate applications.

summary: Assign the same value to count existing output elements. It does not create destination storage. A nonpositive count performs no assignments.
signature:
template<class OutputIt, class Size, class T>
OutputIt fill_n(OutputIt first, Size count, const T& value);
parameters:
- `first`: writable output start.
- `count`: element count.
- `value`: value to assign.
returns: The iterator after the assigned elements. Exactly max(count, 0) assignments.

summary: Sort a writable random-access range while preserving the relative order of equivalent elements. The comparator must define a strict weak ordering.
signature:
template<class RandomIt>
void stable_sort(RandomIt first, RandomIt last);
parameters: - Writable random-access range; comparator overloads accept a strict weak ordering.
returns: No return value. N log N comparisons with sufficient extra memory, otherwise up to N log-squared N comparisons in C++17.

summary: Put the smallest middle-first elements into a sorted prefix. The remaining suffix has unspecified order. Requires a valid writable random-access range.
signature:
template<class RandomIt>
void partial_sort(RandomIt first, RandomIt middle, RandomIt last);
parameters:
- `[first, middle)`: prefix to fill with the smallest sorted elements.
- `[first, last)`: complete input range.
returns: No return value. Approximately N log M comparisons for N input elements and a prefix of M elements.

summary: Place the element that would occupy nth in a sorted range at that position and partition around it. Neither side is necessarily sorted. Requires random-access iterators and a strict weak ordering.
signature:
template<class RandomIt>
void nth_element(RandomIt first, RandomIt nth, RandomIt last);
parameters: - Writable range and the desired sorted position, which may equal last.
returns: No return value. The non-policy overload has linear average complexity.

summary: Find the first element greater than value according to the comparison. The range must be partitioned for this search; a sorted range using the same ordering satisfies the precondition.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class T>
ForwardIt upper_bound(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, const T& value);
parameters: - Partitioned range and search value.
returns: The first matching position or last. Logarithmic comparisons; traversal may be linear without random-access iterators.

summary: Find the half-open subrange of elements equivalent to value. The input must satisfy both lower_bound and upper_bound partitioning requirements, normally by being sorted with the same ordering.
signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class T>
std::pair<ForwardIt, ForwardIt> equal_range(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, const T& value);
parameters: - Partitioned input range and search value.
returns: A pair of lower and upper bounds; an absent value produces an empty subrange. Logarithmic comparisons, with potentially linear traversal.

summary: An owning input file stream for char text or bytes. Construction can open a file; failure is reported through stream state unless exceptions are enabled. Destruction closes the associated file.

- File streams additionally provide `open()`, `close()` and `is_open()`.
- String streams provide `str()` to access their buffer contents.

summary: An owning output file stream for char data. The usual output-only open mode creates or truncates the file; use app when writes must append. Check stream state, including after close, for output errors.
members:

summary: A file stream supporting both input and output. The default in|out mode normally requires an existing file. Specify trunc to create a fresh read/write file, and use positioning or flushing as required when changing direction.

signature:
bool is_directory(const path& file);
bool is_directory(const path& file, std::error_code& error) noexcept;
parameters: - Path arguments identify filesystem objects. Error-code overloads take a std::error_code output reference where provided.
returns: true only for a directory. Missing paths return false; other errors follow the selected overload.

summary: Create one directory. Its parent must already exist; use create_directories when intermediate parents are needed. A path that already names a directory is not an error.
parameters: - Path arguments identify filesystem objects. Error-code overloads take a std::error_code output reference where provided.
returns: true if a new directory was created, false if it was already a directory. Errors throw filesystem_error; error_code overloads are also available.

summary: Create missing intermediate directories and the final directory. Existing directories are accepted. This does not guarantee that the whole operation is atomic.
parameters: - Path arguments identify filesystem objects. Error-code overloads take a std::error_code output reference where provided.
returns: true if the final directory was created, false if it already existed. Errors follow the throwing or error_code overload.

summary: Remove a single file, symlink or empty directory. A symlink itself is removed, not its target. This is not recursive; use remove_all only when recursive deletion is intended.
signature:
bool remove(const path& file);
bool remove(const path& file, std::error_code& error) noexcept;
parameters: - Path arguments identify filesystem objects. Error-code overloads take a std::error_code output reference where provided.
returns: true if an object was removed, false if none existed. Errors follow the selected reporting overload.

summary: Rename or move an object as if by the corresponding POSIX rename rules, including supported replacement cases. Cross-filesystem moves can fail. Error-code overloads allow reporting without exceptions.
signature: void rename(const path& oldName, const path& newName);
parameters: - Path arguments identify filesystem objects. Error-code overloads take a std::error_code output reference where provided.
returns: No return value. The throwing overload reports filesystem_error on failure.

summary: Get or change the process-wide working directory. Changing it affects relative paths throughout the process, including other threads; prefer explicit paths when possible.
signature:
path current_path();
void current_path(const path& directory);
parameters: - Path arguments identify filesystem objects. Error-code overloads take a std::error_code output reference where provided.
returns: The getter returns an absolute path for the current directory. The setter returns no value; errors follow the chosen overload.

summary: A single-pass input iterator over entries in one directory, excluding the special dot and dot-dot entries. Traversal order is unspecified. A default-constructed iterator is the end sentinel; incrementing or dereferencing an end iterator is invalid. Available since C++17.
members:
- Construction with a path begins enumeration.
- `operator*`, `operator->`: inspect the current directory_entry.
- `operator++`: advance.
- Copies need not be independent. Visibility of concurrent directory changes is unspecified.

summary: Return the final filename component without accessing the filesystem. A trailing separator can produce an empty filename.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: A path containing the filename component.

summary: Return the filename with its last extension removed. Hidden-file and special dot-name rules differ from merely splitting at the first dot.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: A path containing the stem component.

summary: Return the last filename extension including its leading dot. An ordinary filename without an extension produces an empty path.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: The extension as a path, or an empty path.

summary: Return the path with its final filename component removed, without looking up the filesystem.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: A path representing the parent portion.

summary: Test whether the path stores no characters. This says nothing about whether the filesystem object exists or has contents.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: true when the stored path is empty.

summary: Test whether the stored path is absolute according to the platform path rules. On Windows, a drive letter alone is not necessarily an absolute path.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: true if the path is absolute; no filesystem lookup is performed.

summary: Obtain a narrow-character representation of a path. Encoding and conversion behavior depend on the platform; do not assume this is always UTF-8. Conversion can allocate or fail.
parameters: No parameters for these overloads.
returns: A new narrow string representing the native path.
